title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 27 | Week 12 vs. Washington Commanders
headline: Carson Beck (back spasms) and Jon Gaines are out Sunday, so Josh Johnson starts at QB against Washington, with Beck's return possible next week.
summary: LaFleur opened by ruling out Carson Beck and Jon Gaines for Sunday. Beck's back spasms are improving, but the coach called him frustrated, and next week is still a possibility for his return. Josh Johnson gets a full week of practice this time. LaFleur said Johnson is more comfortable with the huddle and cadence, but he is still new, so the focus is on building offensive line continuity over the final six weeks. He singled out Harrison Wallace III as a bright spot from last week's game. LaFleur declined to say where one receiver ranks on the depth chart behind another, and the names are unclear in the captions. He also had no timeline for Jeremiyah Love's return to the field and said he would know more Monday or Wednesday. The defensive play-calling duties have changed hands, and he teased unspecified wrinkles for Sunday. He praised Jayden Daniels's composure and Sonny Styles's athleticism, and named Dante Stills as the defender who has stood out.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 12 Media Availability | Friday, November 27th | Press Conference
headline: Left guard Matthew Bergeron (back) looks unlikely to play, with Kyle Hinton the likely fill-in. Beaux Collins is trending toward more opportunities.
summary: Stefanski said Bergeron's back injury dates to the previous game, and the team knew going into the bye that he might miss this week. He is still 'working through it,' but the coach is already preparing for Kyle Hinton to play left guard and said he is comfortable with that. He called the opposing defense excellent and well coached, and said blocking its pressure packages in both the run and pass game is the main challenge. On Beaux Collins, he said the receiver keeps performing well in practice and will earn more opportunities, though his role depends on personnel packages and the game plan. He also spoke at length about the bye-week review of slow starts, saying there is no single cause and no quick fix. He said the team needs a sound plan so players can play fast early, and that falling behind hurts a run-heavy offense. He praised LaCale London's energy and power as a run defender. He also described the Friday high school highlight tape ritual and said rookie Avieon Terrell is handling a season of injuries and ups and downs well.

injuries.detail: Hurt his back in the previous game and did not practice on Friday. Stefanski said he is 'working through it' but is already planning for Kyle Hinton at left guard. He did not rule Bergeron out explicitly.
Stefanski said the rookie has been through a lot of injuries and is bouncing back and handling it well. He gave no specific current injury or status.

signals.note: A line shuffle at left guard could affect run-blocking quality against a strong pressure defense, which matters for the run game.

title: Jesse Minter Rules Out Three Ravens for Texans Game
headline: Ravens rule out Hawkins and, per the captions, guard Olaivavega Ioane ("Vega"); Marlon Humphrey will play, and Jacoby Brissett got strong praise.
summary: Minter opened by saying three players will be out against Houston: Jaylinn Hawkins, a player whose name the captions garbled, and a guard the captions render as "venga", most likely Olaivavega Ioane (nickname "Vega"). He said the guard's injury shouldn't be long term but the timeline is uncertain, and he noted the bye next week helps. Minter praised Jacoby Brissett's professionalism, command of the huddle and the operation. He said Brissett has played well enough in two games to give the team chances to win, and that the players around him need to play better. The interior line is unsettled with the guard out. Minter said the staff would finalize the plan that afternoon and didn't name a starter. He confirmed Marlon Humphrey will play, said Humphrey has handled his return like a pro, and declined to share the plan for using him. He called Texans edge Will Anderson a game wrecker who must be accounted for on every snap, and praised Clowney as still playing at a high level. Houston may be missing Danielle Hunter and a guy or two up front, which could change over the next day or two. Minter also said the team understands what is at stake but is focusing on its own process and preparation.

title: Joe Brady Addresses The Media Following FINAL-SECOND Win Over Kansas City Chiefs!
headline: Bills won 13-10 in rain and wind with a run-first approach: James Cook was the workhorse, Josh Allen threw for only about 80 yards, and Brady is fully backing Allen.
summary: Brady praised the special teams sequence, a well-fielded kick and then the kicker (Tyler Bass) coming through with two key kicks in terrible conditions after a rough week. He said the run game and James Cook were what the team could hang its hat on in a wind, rain and cold game, with Josh Allen at roughly 80 passing yards. He said the team has to play better, took blame for scoring only 13 points, and cited field position and manageable third downs as the plan. He admitted two red-zone turnovers hurt, but said he is not concerned about Allen, will go down with him every day, and expects to see his best version soon, possibly next week. He praised the defense for wanting to be on the field late against Mahomes and Kansas City, and defended coordinator Jim Leonard's blitz-heavy calls, saying the results now match the process. He also explained his late-game timeout management and noted that Cook scored after a sideline helmet mix-up. No new injury information on skill players was given beyond a reference to the kicker's apparent injury.

injuries.detail: A reporter said he didn't look like himself, and Brady referred to 'the injury' without giving details. He still made the winning kick and the key kick before it.

signals.claim: Cook remains the featured back and the run game is the offense's foundation in bad-weather games.
signals.note: Brady praised Cook for grinding out hard yards and protecting the ball in a game where the passing game was limited, which supports a heavy workload.
signals.quote: James is playing really well. Every one of those yards was really hard to get.

signals.claim: Allen's best form is still ahead, and Brady expects to see it next week.
signals.note: Allen was held to about 80 passing yards and had red-zone turnovers, but Brady fully backs him and expects improved decision-making, so the weather-driven dip looks temporary.
signals.quote: I'm not concerned with Josh Allen.

topics.detail: Brady called the wind, rain and cold a unique combination. He leaned on the run game, field position and manageable third downs, and took blame for scoring only 13 points.

Brady praised the defense for wanting to be on the field in late two-minute situations against Patrick Mahomes. He credited Jim Leonard's blitz-heavy calls and said the defense is playing at a high level.
Brady praised a well-fielded kick that set up the finish and Tyler Bass's two kicks in tough conditions, including the 'not easy' one before the game-winner.
Brady explained that he had a predetermined number for when to call a timeout. He called one right after the Mahomes sack-fumble, and the Bills got the ball back with timeouts intact.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : November 27th, 2026
headline: Browns WR Denzel Boston's Sunday status is still up in the air (quad), so Jerry Jeudy is the main beneficiary. Safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren should see more snaps after his first start.
summary: Monken said the team was hopeful that Denzel Boston plays Sunday but is preparing for him to miss it. The coaches have been giving Boston's reps to the other receivers since the last game, and Monken praised Jerry Jeudy's practice and play. Austin Barber is still dealing with a knee problem from the last game. He did a good amount of work today, and the team is monitoring swelling after practice and expects a clearer picture tomorrow. Monken wants to get safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren on the field more after his first start against Houston, possibly through big nickel or dime packages. He said the opponent moves Maxx Crosby around, though historically Crosby lines up on Cleveland's right. He called Fernando Mendoza a mobile quarterback with plenty of arm talent, and the plan is to make the Raiders one-dimensional and get pressure on third down. Monken declined to comment on the Steelers/Aaron Rodgers news, saying he is focused only on Cleveland. He also gave a long answer on aggressiveness and two-point conversion strategy, explaining that the choice depends on your belief in your own personnel.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week 12 #PHIvsDAL
headline: Cowboys blew a 21-point lead in a 39-38 loss to the Eagles and fell to 5-7. Schottenheimer gave no fantasy-relevant role or injury news, but he defended trusting Dak Prescott on a failed fourth-and-2 in the second half.
summary: Schottenheimer was asked almost entirely about the collapse and his job status, and he offered few specifics on players. He said all three phases had chances to put the game away and failed, and he cited a blocked punt and big plays allowed. He defended going for it on fourth-and-2 because he trusted Dak Prescott and the offense, and said he would make the call again. He said the offense moved the ball up and down the field in the first half but was not good enough in the second. He credited Joe Milton with extending plays and throwing the ball deep, and said Dallas let him escape and did not plaster in coverage. He called the five sacks a positive but said the defense needs to get the quarterback down more. He took responsibility as head coach, said he is not worried about his job status, and said the team has solutions and 11 days to work on scheme and personnel adjustments before the trip to Seattle. He said Dallas will believe in the kicker despite a missed 40-yarder, and a closing remark apparently confirmed that someone had back spasms, but the player was not clear in the transcript.

injuries.detail: At the very end the coach confirmed someone had back spasms, but the question was not captured and the player cannot be identified.

signals.claim: Prescott and the offense remain the preferred option on key short-yardage and fourth-down situations.
signals.note: The coach's trust in Prescott on fourth down suggests an aggressive offense that keeps the ball in his hands in late-game situations.
signals.quote: I wanted the ball in Dak's hands.

topics.detail: Dallas lost a 21-point lead; the coach blamed all three phases, including a blocked punt and big plays allowed.

Joe Milton extended plays and Dallas failed to plaster in coverage. The five sacks were a positive, but the coach wants more pressure and better coverage. Dallas has already changed its defensive play caller and personnel.

The coach went for it on fourth-and-2 because he trusted the offense and said he would make the same call again. He said Dallas has used quarterback sneaks before and that Prescott has a good feel for them.
After a missed 40-yarder, the coach wants to review the whole operation on film but says the team believes in its kicker.
Dallas is 5-7 and the coach says he is not worried about his job. He believes in the locker room and has 11 days to look for solutions.

title: HC Sean Payton following Week 12 vs. Steelers: ‘We’ve got to learn from it’
headline: Broncos fall to 8-3 after a one-dimensional road loss to the Steelers; Sean Payton blames his own play-calling, and J.K. Dobbins' status stays unclear.
summary: Payton called the loss disappointing and put it on himself, saying Denver gave Pittsburgh early chances to build momentum. He said the weather was a factor but not as bad as feared, and that he wanted more balance once the game got to two scores. The Steelers brought pressure, including some zero looks, and played the underneath throws well. Payton said Pittsburgh had a good plan. He pointed to missed short-yardage chances early and to a slow-developing screen that he regretted calling. He explained Jonah Coleman's quiet day by the low snap count and time of possession rather than anything new in Pittsburgh's rush looks. He defended Bo Nix against questions about road and playoff weather, saying the one-dimensional offense was more on him than on Nix. He said Nix will bounce back after the pick six, and that it is the staff's job to give him chances to do so. Asked about Dobbins for Monday, he gave no update. He also explained the field-goal decision, citing wind direction and field position.

injuries.detail: Listed as DNP this week for a personal matter, not an injury. Payton gave no update on his status when asked.

signals.note: Coleman was bottled up in a game with low snap counts and little time of possession, and Payton did not suggest his role is changing.
signals.quote: the time of possession and the snaps weren't really high

signals.claim: Nix will bounce back from the pick six, and Denver will work to give him chances to do so.
signals.note: Payton took the blame for the one-dimensional offense and backed Nix in bad weather, so there is no sign of a confidence problem despite the pick six.
signals.quote: he'll bounce back and it's our job to give them those opportunities

signals.note: Payton gave no update on Dobbins' status beyond saying it will come later, so his availability remains uncertain.
signals.quote: Yeah, we'll see when that comes.

topics.detail: Denver expected a weather game, though Payton said conditions were not as bad as feared. He wanted more balance on offense and said it became hard once the game reached two scores.
The Steelers got quite a bit of pressure, including some zero looks, and took away the underneath throws. Payton said they had a good plan.

Payton was disappointed in the early short-yardage plays. He regretted calling a slow-developing screen on the first score, and said the pick six and the defensive score gave Pittsburgh a big momentum swing.
Payton said the late long field-goal attempt was a different situation from the early punt. The wind was 40 to their right and 35 to their left, and he thought the kicker did not hit it well.
Asked about losing by ten or more to all three winning teams Denver has played on the road, Payton said he is focused on next week. He noted Denver is 8-3 after a good schedule.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 12 final update, Colts vs. Giants
headline: Anthony Richardson starts for the Colts vs. the Giants; five Colts are out (Ward, McGowan, Travis, Mallory, Tillery) and LT Bernhard Raimann is cleared from the concussion protocol.
summary: Steichen ruled out Charvarius Ward, Seth McGowan, Jalen Travis, Will Mallory and Jerry Tillery for Sunday's game against the Giants. He added that Bernhard Raimann has cleared concussion protocol. Most of the session was about Anthony Richardson, who is getting his opportunity as the starter. Steichen said the excitement is visible in him and his teammates, that he had a great week of preparation and a good practice today, and that he even came in after Thanksgiving to watch tape with the staff. He called the situation unique given the trade request but said the team is glad Richardson is here and getting to prove himself. He said the team wants to see Richardson take the easy completions rather than rely only on splash plays, and that he has improved at that over his career. On the Giants, he praised J.J. McCarthy's athleticism, scrambling, arm and tight-window throws, and called Abdul Carter a freak who has been humming off the edge and needs a specific plan. Asked about coaching-job speculation, he said he blocks it out and focuses on preparing the team.

title: Coen on Parker Washington Game Status, "Next Man Up" & Readiness for Titans | Press Conference
headline: Parker Washington (shoulder) is out for the Titans game and week-to-week, so expect Josh Cameron, Travis Hunter and the other pass catchers to absorb his targets. Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) is a true game-time decision, with Ameer Abdullah next in line.
summary: Coen said Parker Washington hurt his shoulder in Thursday's practice and will miss this game, with a week-to-week timeline. The game plan was mostly set, so the staff only tweaked formations and is leaning on a 'next man up' approach with simplified concepts. Josh Cameron was singled out for a bigger offensive role, and Coen said Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers, Brenton Strange, Nate Boerkircher and the backs all need to step up. He said Travis Hunter will definitely see some offensive action this week, in some passing situations and also as a run-game blocker. Coen said Washington was Trevor Lawrence's favorite target and his contested catches will be missed, so Lawrence is being pushed to read the progression, trust his rhythm and throw to the open man. Tuten's availability is uncertain: Coen would look at him in the final practice and said he might give him a go but wasn't sure. If Tuten can't play, Coen said Ameer Abdullah would take a bigger share of the backfield, along with the rest of the RB room. On the offensive line, Walker Little and Robert Hainsey are working back from injuries, another lineman was described as returning with fresh legs, and Wyatt Milum and Daniel Faalele are both handling jumbo reps. Coen said he is confident in the line's depth and in rookie Emmanuel Pregnon, who has played a lot.

title: Andy Reid: 'Our Defense Played Their Tails Off' | Postgame Press Conference - NFL Week 12
headline: Jalen Royals and Trey Smith both left the loss to Buffalo with left ankle sprains, and Reid blamed penalties, not the run/pass balance, for the offense stalling.
summary: Reid opened by saying Jalen Royals sprained his left ankle and that Trey Smith had the same injury. He gave no timeline for either. He blamed the loss on too many offensive penalties, especially in the red zone. Two penalties plus a missed field goal hurt the team, and he took responsibility for the lack of discipline. He disagreed with the replay ruling that made a Rashee Rice catch incomplete, saying Rice controlled the ball and the evidence was not clear and obvious. He admitted special teams need to be better and said field position mattered, but he still trusts the special teams leadership. On the kicker, he said he will review everything and make no decision right now. He praised the defense for holding Josh Allen and the Bills' offense down and giving the offense chances. He said the 20 rushing attempts were fine given the many three-and-outs, so run/pass balance was not the problem. He said he does not see a need to add receivers and thinks the room is fine.

injuries.detail: Sprained his left ankle in the game; Reid gave no timeline.

title: Jim Harbaugh on His Confidence in DJ Uiagalelei Ahead of His First Start
headline: DJ Uiagalelei makes his first NFL start for the Chargers in Week 12 vs. New England, with Justin Herbert out (concussion on the injury report); Harbaugh voiced full confidence in him.
summary: Harbaugh opened by saying he is excited for DJ Uiagalelei's first NFL start. He said DJ has been diligent and prepared all season, and that taking the first-team reps this week has helped. He said teammates have real confidence in DJ and that the team is not making a big deal of the change. Harbaugh said DJ's snaps against Houston after Justin Herbert left that game helped, since he got live action and had success. On first-start nerves, he said the butterflies are similar whether it is a first or hundredth start, and that the first contact usually settles them. Reporters then asked about the number of soft-tissue injuries. Harbaugh defended the strength and conditioning staff under Ben Herbert as the best in the business. He said the team tracks the data, saw a spike in hamstring injuries after zero in training camp and the first five games, and called the current injuries mostly contact-related, with a lot of ankles and knees. He named Derwin James as the one long-term soft-tissue case that stands out, and said Brenen Thompson's has been a hamstring since about game five.

title: Klint Kubiak provides injury update, talks final prep for SNF vs. Browns

summary: Kubiak ruled out DTs Adam Butler, Tonka Hemingway and Tim Keenan, plus center Jackson Powers-Johnson. JJ Pegues, Brock Bowers and a third player whose name was garbled are questionable. Bowers did not practice Friday after being limited and wearing ankle tape earlier in the week. Kubiak called his status a 'moving target' and said they have 48 hours to see how he plays. He said the bye next week could factor into the decision, but the team wants everyone who is ready to play. Kubiak expects inclement weather (wind, rain, a grass field) and said the team has prepared for it. Asked whether weather boosts Mike Washington Jr.'s role, he said it could, but that the team is counting on Washington and Ashton Jeanty to take a big load either way. He expressed confidence in the depleted DT group and said he still counts on veteran Folorunso Fatukasi. He also named rookie QB Fernando Mendoza a captain simply because he is the quarterback, said Mendoza leads by production, and called Cleveland very poised in late-game situations. He said punt protection was a point of emphasis after last week's breakdown, and he mentioned a play-action 'guitar fake' concept. A player was ruled out after an injury at Friday's practice, and Kubiak said more details would come Saturday.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Injury Updates, Falcons Game, Special Teams Contributions, Kirk Cousins’ Leadership
headline: Addison, Darrisaw and Rodgers are out vs. ATL; Van Demark starts at LT, Cousins remains the trusted starter, and Kyler Murray is likely the backup.

Harrison Smith is questionable with a thigh injury, but he got some work in today. Kyler Murray practiced fully enough this week to be the likely backup, with Carson Wentz third. He also praised Cousins' leadership with the young skill players (Myles Price, Tai Felton, Jeshaun Jones, Gavin Bartholomew, Ben Yurosek) and his sound approach to avoiding sacks while still hunting explosive plays. He also praised special teams coordinator Matt Daniels and the unit's depth.

title: Kellen Moore talks injury report, Cincinnati | Saints vs. Bengals 2026 NFL Week 12
headline: TE Juwan Johnson is out and Noah Fant is questionable (calf), which would leave Oscar Delp as the lead TE; Fuaga and Richards are also questionable.
summary: Moore ruled TE Juwan Johnson out for Week 12 with a hamstring injury; he did not practice. Fant's soreness was reported Friday morning but had been lingering, and Moore didn't commit either way on his availability. If Fant can't play, Oscar Delp is the top tight end available. Moore called Delp physical and productive when he has played, and said to expect more opportunities for him. Mason Murphy drew praise for his tackle play last week, which matters if the line is short. Erik McCoy is back as the starting center, and Moore praised his leadership. Moore said rookie WR Jordyn Tyson had a great week of practice and that his opportunities will keep growing, while pointing out that last week's target volume was a function of opportunity rather than a problem. He called Travis Etienne's ability to reach the edge an asset, but said finding edge runs in the game plan is still a work in progress. He also said QB Tyler Shough has been effective in the drop-back game, which he compared to the Bengals' early-down approach.

title: Coach John Harbaugh provides final updates before Week 12 matchup
headline: Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are the featured slot weapons, and Harbaugh says opponents have trouble matching up with them. Shelby Harris is sick and his status is unclear.
summary: Harbaugh said practice was good and the team is locked in for Sunday. A player asked about right after Harris, whose name is garbled in the captions, was a full participant, and Harbaugh said the team will monitor his workload. Harbaugh said Malik Nabers has produced from the slot on relatively few snaps there because he is hard to match up with, and that Isaiah Likely has also been very good in the slot. He said the scheme is built to get both open and that opponents will know it too. Harbaugh also described a short-yardage package (fourth-and-1 and third-and-1) that has worked, started to take a rep off J.J. He said Likely's current role is about what he envisioned from their years together in Baltimore, praised his route-running and his involvement in game planning, and called him a premier leader. The rest of the session was general talk about close games, replay confusion on catches, and his 2008 first win.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: November 26, 2026
headline: Joe Milton III played an outstanding game in the 39-38 Thanksgiving win over Dallas, but DeVonta Smith was hurting after the game, so watch his status.
summary: Sirianni was exhausted and thrilled after the 39-38 Thanksgiving win over the Cowboys, praising how hard the team fought until time ran out. He called Joe Milton III's game outstanding. He said Milton was composed, moved on from mistakes (including an interception) and made the defense pay when it brought extra rushers. He highlighted Milton's unique arm strength and his ability to layer throws against Cover 2, including a long completion to DeVonta Smith. Sirianni said the offense was not limited with other quarterbacks, but that Milton's arm is a unique trait. Smith showed toughness by finishing the game while visibly hurting, to the point that he asked Sirianni to put him down after being picked up. Sirianni defended his decision to go for two when down 14 and said he sticks to his process rather than the outcome. Jake Elliott kicked the game-winner, which Sirianni didn't watch, and the team's "keep swimming" message about fighting through adversity framed the win.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Gives Final Updates Ahead Of Week 12 at 49ers
headline: Sam Darnold is practicing fully and healthy, Leonard Williams and Charles Cross return, and Jarran Reed is out for the Week 12 trip to San Francisco.
summary: Macdonald said three players are listed as out and that Sam Darnold is healthy after a full Wednesday practice, though he added that nobody on the roster is fully healthy this late in the season. Leonard Williams is back from his absence and was described as possibly the team's best player, someone who can wreck games from the inside. His practice week was called tremendous, but Macdonald said there are still things the team is taking under consideration, so a snap count is possible. Jarran Reed will miss the game. He finished the last game but hasn't been able to get past the injury, and his availability next week is uncertain. Rylie Mills and a nose tackle whose name was garbled in the captions get the chance to step up. Mills was praised as a physical, hard-working player who communicates well along the line. Charles Cross is returning, which Macdonald called much needed for an offensive line that has lacked continuity, and he alluded to an 'Abe' (Abraham Lucas) situation. Ernest Jones was praised as the emotional leader and tackle leader who patrols the middle of the defense. Macdonald said the uncertainty over whether Brock Purdy plays did not change preparation, and the 49ers' 21-personnel packages are harder to prepare for because of how they have adjusted around injuries.

title: Shanahan Addresses Purdy’s Ankle, Mac Jones Set for First Start
headline: Brock Purdy is out for Sunday at Seattle with a mid-grade ankle sprain, so Mac Jones makes his first start of the season. Mike Evans is questionable.
summary: Shanahan ruled Purdy out for the Seattle game. He said the ankle sprain was 'more mid than low' (not a high ankle sprain), and it did not heal fast enough by Wednesday, so they shut him down. Surgery is not an option, and Shanahan is 'pretty optimistic' about next week but called it too soon to know. He said the weather played no part in the decision. He expressed strong confidence in Mac Jones, praising his camp and his consistency, and said he is glad they did not trade him, though he said no offers were official. The offensive line is thin: Pleasants (questionable) has practiced only at tackle this week, and Cruz is ready as the swing tackle if needed. A decision on Pleasants comes tomorrow. Carver Willis is the next man up at guard and is not being considered at tackle. Other questionable players are Siran Neal, Upton Stout, Dre Greenlaw and Mike Evans. Jordan Watkins is out. Shanahan called Seattle a Super Bowl-caliber team that is still very capable, so the 49ers have 'our work cut out'. Jones also spoke, saying he feels prepared, expects rain, and that the offense will be simplified a bit for him.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Cordale Flott and Terrell Burgess are out vs. Jacksonville. Everyone else is trending up, and Saleh expects no change in the Gray/Barton linebacker rotation.
summary: Saleh opened by ruling out Cordale Flott and Terrell Burgess, saying everyone else is trending in the right direction pending Friday's practice. At safety, Tony Adams will be available, Isaiah Oliver is in the mix, and a player who sounded like "Hallett" will take the fourth safety role. New arrival Corey Thornton drew early praise for his size, length and work ethic. Fernando Carmona is getting closer to returning, but Saleh does not expect him to be activated yet. At linebacker he expects more of the same from Cedric Gray and Cody Barton. On Jacksonville, he said losing Parker Washington will hurt but he doesn't expect the offense to skip a beat. He praised their weapons and said their quarterback is playing the best football he's seen from him. He said facing them twice in three weeks means a mix of executing better and adding or pulling out game-plan elements. He also wants his young team to learn to finish through late-season soreness, called James Hudson solid in fill-in duty, and praised the kicker's reliability.
